bug: Applied .round(7) to all four columns including CYP2D6, whose shift is zero. The base file stores more precision than 7 dp, so 'adding zero then rounding' perturbed the one column that must stay byte-identical as the built-in control.
found_by: this notebook's own control assertion, on the first execution -- the atol=1e-6 integrity print said exact=True while the exact-equality assert failed, which is why both checks exist
fix: transform only the columns with a non-zero shift; leave CYP2D6 untouched and assert byte-identity of the written text as well as float equality

where: Part 5, the byte-identity control check itself
bug: Compared the CYP2D6 column by a naive comma split on the raw lines. 13 of 750 SMILES carry CXSMILES enhanced-stereo annotations containing a comma (e.g. '|&1:17,19|'), so those fields are CSV-QUOTED and the naive split misaligns every column after SMILES on exactly those rows -- it reported 13 differences that were really the shifted CYP1A2/CYP2C9 values read out of the wrong field.
found_by: the check failing while pandas simultaneously reported exact float equality -- two checks disagreeing is what exposed it
fix: use csv.DictReader. Worth carrying forward as a repo-level hazard: any code in this project that parses a submission CSV by splitting on commas is wrong on those 13 rows.

bug: Grouped the four CYP1A2 roots by their raw float sd_y to find mirror pairs. fsolve returns sd_y to about 1e-9, so mirror partners landed in separate singleton groups and the pair annotation indexed .iloc[1] out of bounds.
found_by: the notebook failing to execute at the figure cell
fix: group on sd_y rounded to 4 dp, and guard the annotation on len(group) == 2

bug: A draft prediction read 'CYP2C9 and CYP3A4 R2 also rise'. The notebook's own Part 4 table contradicts it for CYP3A4: BOTH of its branches lower R2 (~0.651 high, ~0.589 low), because the rise/fall rule needs |b| > delta/2 and CYP3A4's |b| (0.082) is smaller than delta/2 (0.095).
found_by: reading the executed output against the prose -- the same way the two prose errors in the superseded notebook 55 were caught, and the reason this project reads its own output rather than trusting its drafts
fix: state the prediction per isoform, add a direction_test_applies_to block computing |b| against delta/2 for each, and say plainly that the probe resolves CYP3A4 by magnitude rather than by direction
